questions.explanation: A data point is one observation — one piece of information.
questions.misconception: The average is a statistic computed from many points; a data point is just one raw piece of data.

questions.prompt: What two things does a data point usually have?
questions.explanation: A data point typically pairs a label ('Ali') with a value ('150 cm').
questions.misconception: The essential parts are the identity (label) and the measurement (value) — appearance is just how we draw a point.

questions.prompt: Many data points together form a...
questions.explanation: Collecting many data points creates a dataset.
questions.misconception: A single point is just one observation — a collection of many points is a dataset, which charts and statistics summarize.

questions.prompt: How does a data point appear when placed on a line graph?
options: As a dot with a height matching its value
questions.explanation: On a line graph each data point becomes one dot placed by its value.
questions.misconception: Bars group whole categories, axes frame the chart, and legends explain symbols — a single point is just a dot.

questions.prompt: A measurement that is far away from the others in a dataset is every data point too, but is called an...
questions.explanation: A point far from the rest is an outlier — but still one data point.
questions.misconception: The special name for an unusually distant point is outlier; it is not a median or an axis, and it still counts as a point.
